english.title: Threaten a person with an offensive weapon / bladed article / corrosive substance in a private place
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) unlawfully and intentionally, threatened another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), with

(A)_[an offensive weapon within the meaning of section 1 of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953, namely **(..SPECIFY WEAPON..),]_
(B)_[an article to which section 139 of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 applies, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..),]_
(C)_[a corrosive substance, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SUBSTANCE..),]_

in a private place, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), in such a way that there was an immediate risk of serious physical harm to that person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 52(1) and (6) of the Offensive Weapons Act 2019.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) A "corrosive substance" is defined in section 52(8) as a substance that is capable of burning human skin by corrosion.
(ii) 'private place' is defined in section 52(3) and (4) with the latter setting out a different application for a corrosive substance.
(iii) 'serious physical harm' is defined in section 52(5) as harm that amounts to grievous bodily harm for the purposes of the Offences against the Person Act 1861.
(iv) Section 53 permits a search for corrosive substances on school or further education premises.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 4 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force, the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
